- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The naturalization process typically takes around 6-12 months, depending on the local USCIS office and case complexity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The general steps for the naturalization process include determining eligibility, preparing and submitting Form N-400, attending a biometrics appointment, an interview and testing, and an oath ceremony.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Eligibility requirements for naturalization include being at least 18 years old, being a lawful permanent resident for at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to a US citizen), meeting continuous residence and physical presence requirements, demonstrating good moral character, passing English language and civics tests, showing attachment to the US Constitution, and taking the Oath of Allegiance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips for the naturalization process include reviewing N-400 instructions, consulting with an immigration attorney if needed, preparing for tests using USCIS materials, and being honest in the application and interview.
- [FACT] The user is interested in the specific English language skills required for the naturalization test.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The English language skills required for the naturalization test include reading, writing, and speaking basic English.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For the reading portion, the user must read a sentence aloud correctly; for writing, they must write a sentence correctly; and for speaking, they must understand and respond to questions in English.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended resources for preparing for the English language test include USCIS study materials, language learning apps like Duolingo and English Central, and online platforms like USAHello.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The civics test consists of questions about American government, American history, and integrated civics, with up to 10 questions asked from a list of 100 possible questions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Key topics to focus on for the civics test include the Constitution, branches of government, American history, civics and government, and symbols and holidays.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended study resources for the civics test include USCIS materials, online practice tests, and authentic materials like news articles and documentaries.
